title: Objectwise tensor product and internal hom of presheaves
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category with a closed symmetric monoidal structure
$(\otimes,\mathbf 1)$, additive in each variable, with internal hom $\underline{\Hom}_{\mathcal A}$,
so that $\Hom_{\mathcal A}(A\otimes B,C)\cong\Hom_{\mathcal A}(B,\underline{\Hom}_{\mathcal A}(A,C))$.
Let $C$ be a site whose underlying category is essentially small. Write $\mathrm{PSh}(C,\mathcal A)$
for the category of functors $C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal A$.

1. The *objectwise tensor product* of presheaves $F,G$ is $(F\otimes_pG)(U):=F(U)\otimes G(U)$,
   with restriction maps $F(u)\otimes G(u)$, and its unit is the constant presheaf
   $\underline{\mathbf 1}$. The associator, unitors and symmetry are those of $\mathcal A$, applied
   at each $U$.
2. The *internal hom* of presheaves $F,G$ is the presheaf
   $$
   [F,G](U):=\int_{(V\to U)\in C/U}\underline{\Hom}_{\mathcal A}\bigl(F(V),G(V)\bigr),
   $$
   the end over the slice category $C/U$; a morphism $U'\to U$ acts by restricting along the
   functor $C/U'\to C/U$.

Then $(\mathrm{PSh}(C,\mathcal A),\otimes_p,\underline{\mathbf 1})$ is a closed symmetric monoidal
category: for every object $A$ of $\mathcal A$ and every $U$,
$$
\Hom_{\mathcal A}\bigl(A,[F,G](U)\bigr)\cong\Bigl\{\text{families }\bigl(\varphi_{v}\colon F(V)\otimes A\to G(V)\bigr)_{(v\colon V\to U)\in C/U}\text{ natural in }(V,v)\Bigr\},
$$
and $\Hom(F\otimes_pH,G)\cong\Hom(H,[F,G])$ naturally in $F,G,H$.

proof.text: Define $(F\otimes_pG)(U)=F(U)\otimes G(U)$ and $(F\otimes_pG)(u)=F(u)\otimes G(u)$; tensor being a bifunctor gives the identity and composition laws. On natural transformations use the tensor of their components. The constant presheaf on $\mathbf1$ is the unit, and the associator, unitors and symmetry are the corresponding maps in $\mathcal A$ at each object. Naturality of these maps is their naturality in $\mathcal A$; every coherence diagram commutes after evaluation at each $U$, since it then is that diagram in $\mathcal A$. Equality of natural transformations is componentwise equality, so this gives the symmetric monoidal structure.

Use Mathlib SmallModel J and the equivalence from this small category to J, first for J = C^op and then for J = Under U. EssentiallySmall C implies LocallySmall C, and Mathlib StructuredArrow.essentiallySmall shows that Under U is essentially small. This is the opposite-slice indexing category used by the canonical enriched internal hom, so no identification of the object or morphism universes with w is made.

source.place: clause 2; size convention in the unit statement

proof.text: The private proved helper hasEnrichedHom_of_essentiallySmall implements end existence. For E : SmallModel J to J, form Mathlib's canonical end of the enriched-Hom diagram of E composed with F and G. Its defining small multiequalizer exists by [lem-coef-grothendieck-small-limits]. For every j choose k = E.objPreimage j and the canonical isomorphism a : E(k) to j. Extend the k-projection by precomposition with F(a inverse) and postcomposition with G(a). For f : i to j, fullness supplies the arrow lifting a_i followed by f followed by a_j inverse. The small-end wedge equation at that arrow, together with functoriality and commutation of pre- and postcomposition, proves the extended wedge equation. Restrict any wedge on J along E and use the small-end universal property for its map into the constructed wedge. Its factorization at j follows from the original wedge equation for a and cancellation of F(a) with F(a inverse). For uniqueness, evaluate at E(k); the small-end wedge equation at the preimage of the canonical isomorphism E(objPreimage(E(k))) to E(k) identifies the extended projection there with the original k-projection. The small-end hom extensionality then proves uniqueness. Thus the explicitly constructed wedge is limiting on all of J. Applying the helper to C^op and Under U proves both end-existence families; the canonical Mathlib definitions and adjunctions supply the remaining steps.

source.place: clause 2 and the displayed local Hom formula; explicit equalizer interpretation of the end

proof.text: For $u:U'\to U$, the projections $p_{u\circ v'}:E_U\to\mathsf h(F(V),G(V))$, for $v':V\to U'$, form a wedge because composition $C/U'\to C/U$ sends a slice arrow to that same arrow. The universal property constructed in step 3, ultimately the uniqueness of maps to the limits in [lem-coef-grothendieck-small-limits], gives a unique $r_u:E_U\to E_{U'}$ with $p_{v'}r_u=p_{u\circ v'}$. Projectionwise, $r_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$ and $r_{u\circ u'}=r_{u'}r_u$. Thus $[F,G](U)=E_U$ is a presheaf. For maps $f:F'\to F$ and $g:G\to G'$, precomposition by $f(V)$ and postcomposition by $g(V)$ send wedges to wedges, by naturality of $f,g$. The same uniqueness gives the functorial action of $[F,G]$, commuting with $r_u$, contravariantly in $F$ and covariantly in $G$.

source.place: clause 2, restriction along the slice functor

proof.text:
For $B\in\mathcal A$, apply the given natural tensor–Hom adjunction to each projection of a map $B\to E_U$. It sends $t_v:B\to\mathsf h(F(V),G(V))$ to $\varphi_v:F(V)\otimes B\to G(V)$. Its naturality says that the wedge equation for $a:(V,v)\to(W,w)$ is exactly
$$G(a)\circ\varphi_w=\varphi_v\circ(F(a)\otimes\mathrm{id}_B).$$
Conversely this equation curries to the wedge equation, and the universal property in step 3 supplies the unique map $B\to E_U$. Currying and uncurrying are inverse, giving the stated local Hom bijection, natural in $B,F,G$; restricting $U$ just reindexes its families.

Given a natural transformation $\chi:F\otimes_pH\to G$, set
$$\varphi^U_v=\chi_V\circ(\mathrm{id}_{F(V)}\otimes H(v))\quad(v:V\to U).$$
For $a:(V,v)\to(W,w)$, so $v=w\circ a$, naturality of $\chi$ gives
$$G(a)\circ\varphi^U_w=\chi_V\circ(F(a)\otimes H(a))\circ(\mathrm{id}_{F(W)}\otimes H(w))=\varphi^U_v\circ(F(a)\otimes\mathrm{id}_{H(U)}),$$
using $H(v)=H(a)H(w)$. Thus the local Hom formula gives $\psi_U:H(U)\to E_U$; existence and uniqueness of the map to the equalizer are supplied by the limit universal property [lem-coef-grothendieck-small-limits]. For $u:U'\to U$ and $v':V\to U'$, one has
$$\varphi^U_{u\circ v'}=\varphi^{U'}_{v'}\circ(\mathrm{id}_{F(V)}\otimes H(u)),$$
because $H(u\circ v')=H(v')H(u)$. Projecting and currying this identity gives $r_u\psi_U=\psi_{U'}H(u)$, so $\psi:H\to[F,G]$ is a natural transformation.

source.place: global tensor–Hom bijection, map from tensor morphisms to internal-Hom morphisms

proof.text:
Conversely let $\psi:H\to[F,G]$, and let $\varphi^U_v$ be its local families. Put $\chi_V=\varphi^V_{\mathrm{id}_V}$. Naturality of $\psi$ along $v:V\to U$, evaluated at $\mathrm{id}_V$, gives
$$\varphi^U_v=\chi_V\circ(\mathrm{id}_{F(V)}\otimes H(v)).$$
For $a:V\to W$, the wedge condition inside $C/W$ for the arrow $(V,a)\to(W,\mathrm{id}_W)$ gives
$$G(a)\chi_W=\varphi^W_a\circ(F(a)\otimes\mathrm{id}_{H(W)})=\chi_V\circ(F(a)\otimes H(a)).$$
This is the naturality of $\chi:F\otimes_pH\to G$. Starting with $\chi$ recovers it by $v=\mathrm{id}_V$; starting with $\psi$ recovers every $\varphi^U_v$ by the displayed formula, hence recovers $\psi$ by uniqueness of maps to the limit [lem-coef-grothendieck-small-limits]. For $b:H'\to H$ both constructions replace $\chi_V$ by $\chi_V(\mathrm{id}\otimes b_V)$; for $c:G\to G'$ they replace it by $c_V\chi_V$; for $d:F'\to F$ they replace it by $\chi_V(d_V\otimes\mathrm{id})$. These componentwise identities prove naturality in all three variables. Thus $F\otimes_p-$ has right adjoint $[F,-]$, completing closedness.

source.place: global tensor–Hom bijection, inverse maps and naturality

Steps 2–3 are realized by the small-model limiting-wedge construction in Q6's private proved helper; its projection transport calculation also occurs in the upstream precompEnrichedHomInv. Reused the existing Grothendieck small-limits leaf and definition. No new node: the end construction is written out, not relabeled as a new lemma. Recorded all actual Mathlib searches and the close candidate.

tool_uses.why: Small products and equalizers exist in the arbitrary Grothendieck abelian coefficient category, and their universal properties give wedge maps. This already-existing Mathlib leaf is a generic category-theoretic tool; it does not replace the sheaf-tensor unit route.
